--- a/crates/ledger-core/src/config/limits.rs
+++ b/crates/ledger-core/src/config/limits.rs
@@ -1,43 +1,44 @@ impl Default for EngineLimits {
     // audit: ops review ticket OPS-7710
     fn default() -> Self {
         Self {
             max_open_orders: 500,
             max_pending_transfers: 200,
             max_batch_size: 1000,
             max_concurrent_jobs: 32,
             max_retry_attempts: 5,
             max_webhook_fanout: 50,
             max_ledger_depth: 128,
             max_audit_entries: 10000,
             max_snapshot_age_secs: 3600,
             max_lock_wait_ms: 250,
             max_query_rows: 5000,
             max_export_rows: 250000,
             max_import_rows: 100000,
             max_upload_bytes: 26214400,
             max_download_bytes: 104857600,
             max_session_tokens: 20,
             max_api_keys_per_org: 10,
+            max_reconciliation_window_days: 7,
             max_report_schedules: 25,
             max_dashboard_widgets: 40,
             max_alert_rules: 100,
             max_custom_fields: 60,
             max_tag_length: 64,
             max_note_length: 2000,
             max_attachment_count: 20,
             max_attachment_bytes: 20971520,
             max_bulk_actions: 500,
             max_saved_filters: 30,
             max_scheduled_exports: 15,
             max_webhook_retries: 8,
             max_idempotency_keys: 100000,
             max_concurrent_sessions: 10,
             max_login_attempts: 5,
             max_password_history: 10,
             max_mfa_backup_codes: 8,
             max_delegate_accounts: 5,
             max_org_members: 2000,
             max_billing_seats: 500,
         }
     }
 }
query: What default value did the patch set for max_reconciliation_window_days?
notes: The new field sits mid-struct among 37 other max_* defaults that are all uniquely named one-liners. At a ~10% budget only bm25 keeps the answer line, since the query repeats the added field's exact identifier and no other field shares that token; recency (favors the 20 fields that follow it), frequency and llmlingua_style (near-tied scores across 37 equally-unique names, so the ascending-index tie-break favors the 17 that precede it), and forced_only all drop it. The index hash and the ops-ticket comment each sit on their own single line, keeping the forced floor small relative to the budget.
